The finite-history interface p receives time t, exactly Fin t past whole losses, Fin(t+1) actual outputs through Xt, and the current whole loss. Nat.rec appends the actual shared nearest projection, output reads the last point and selected calls this p on this actual history. No future losses, next output or comparator is an explicit policy input. p/initialization/schedule are fixed exogenous parameters; prefix comparisons keep p/x1 fixed and past whole losses/rates equal. This is deterministic pathwise full information, not an executable finite-query oracle, randomized law, filtration/measurability/independence theorem or certification of how external parameters were selected.
